composers_checked.name: Stamitz, Johann
composers_checked.note: Floor from MusicBrainz, Apple Music and the MusicWeb review of ARS38185; only Op. 1 No. 2 has a one-to-a-part recording. Gap check against IMSLP's full Stamitz list (57 pages) and Wikipedia: no further in-scope chamber works.

composers_checked.name: Albrechtsberger, Johann Georg
composers_checked.note: Floor from Apple Music, BnF, MusicWeb and the Hungaroton booklets HCD 32647 and 32653. Thirteen works added that IMSLP lacks (Op. 7 Nos. 4-6; six pieces of Hungaroton HCD 32647; four pieces of Laborie "Entre ciel et terre"). No Weinmann thematic catalogue online, so the gap check rests on recordings and the de.wikipedia list.

note: Stamitz: only Op. 1 No. 2 has a one-to-a-part recording (Der Musikalische Garten, ARS38185); Op. 4 Nos. 3 and 5 are on a Camerata Berolinensis disc whose size I could not find (string-orchestra question). Albrechtsberger: kept Op. 9 Nos. 1-3 (Belvedere Trio Wien, Hungaroton HCD 32109; No. 1 also Dresden Philharmonic String Trio, Genuin), the Divertimento in F for violin, cello and bass (Hungaroton) and Op. 21 Nos. 1-6, which the Authentic Quartet recorded as 'Op. 16' (the HCD 32653 booklet gives the keys and says the set was published as Op. 21). Gap check, works IMSLP lacks: Op. 7 Nos. 4-6 (Hungaroton HCD 32495; Nos. 1-3 may be the DTÖ quartets in D, A and F, unconfirmed); six chamber pieces with flute on Hungaroton HCD 32647 (scorings from the booklet; the Divertimento in C and the Notturno are described only as 'flute quartet', read as flute, violin, viola, cello); four pieces on Laborie 'Entre ciel et terre' (Quatuor Mosaïques, Ensemble baroque de Limoges/C. Coin): two string trios, a divertimento for viola, cello and violone, and a D-minor sextet sonata whose players per part are not confirmed (low confidence; it may be one of the Op. 13 sextets). Not added: the Jew's-harp concerto and the Sonata II a due cori on the Laborie disc (Jew's harp not in the vocabulary; scoring of the double-choir sonata unknown); the Sonata in C 'pro festo Paschalis' (HCD 32653; church sonata with harpsichord continuo, scoring beyond the continuo not found); the Concertino a 5 in E-flat (original for trumpet and strings, Argo/Wilbraham; the 2008 Talitman version for flute, violin, viola, cello and harp looks like an arrangement); the Divertimento in D for two violas and double bass (named in the de.wikipedia list; no recording found). Quatuor Rincontro (Zig-Zag ZZT 091003) also plays an 'Adagio et fugue op. 24 no 4', not matched to any IMSLP page. Levels are estimates from style and recording timings; no scores were read.
